A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KVP research, with matching authors, core method, and retained experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, supervised-learning ablations, qualitative analyses, and latency measurements for KVP, including Qwen and Phi-4 experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds RULER-128K, bilingual passage retrieval, JudgeQ comparisons, and analyses of supervised objectives and head specialization.

M1.justification: Section 3.1.1 corrects the stated normalized training reward from R/R* to the negative cost ratio -C/C*. This changes the written optimization objective, while the per-head MLPs, inputs, Plackett-Luce/Gumbel sampling, and RLOO procedure remain. The PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes or retraining.

E1.justification: v2 adds RULER evaluation at 128K context length and LongBench passage retrieval in English and Chinese, substantially extending input-length, task, and language coverage. ARC-Challenge remains in Appendix A.7 rather than being removed; other original benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds evaluated JudgeQ comparisons on RULER-128K, English/Chinese passage retrieval, and BoolQ. Section 4.2 adds pointwise regression, RankNet, ListNet, and weighted Soft-Sort alongside the existing Soft-Sort comparator, substantially broadening comparisons with learned approaches.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates single compression after prefill using attention-mask emulation. v2 retains that setting but introduces chunked prefill with repeated eviction and physical tensor compaction for long-context evaluations. It also revises the stated meaning of plotted -R^b from cumulative evicted importance to an individual rank's normalized AUC contribution.

E4.justification: The three-learning-rate Soft-Sort study is replaced by a comparison of five supervised objectives. New Appendices A.5-A.6 analyze importance-distribution heterogeneity, regression ranking errors, and agreement among 112 head-specific policies, adding substantial evidence about objective choice and specialization.

E5.justification: Figure 10 newly reports mean ranks with ±1 standard-deviation bands and variance across 112 heads on one sample. These describe inter-head variation, not uncertainty across training runs. The latency benchmark's averaging over 30 runs is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds long-context, retrieval, JudgeQ, and head-analysis results. The replacement ablation finds Soft-Sort close to RL over most budgets, unlike v1's broadly poor surrogate results. BoolQ scores also change: KVP-S at 20 tokens rises from approximately 72% in v1 Figure 3 to 79% in v2 Figure 4, without an explained cause. Most original appendix curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes the claim of NP-hardness even for linear rewards and grounds nestedness in the additive reward rather than general task utility. Section 3.1.1 corrects reward normalization and derives the rank-weighted AUC expression, while redefining R^b. Proposition 1 and its appendix proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain offline, per-head RL ranking with a budget-agnostic reward. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the stated generalization scope explicitly to 128K contexts, or 32 times training length, and foreground passage retrieval alongside retained downstream tasks.

C2.justification: The explanation for supervised-ranking weaknesses changes from temperature and gradient problems to heavy-tailed importance distributions and magnitude-sensitive versus rank-only loss tradeoffs. v2 adds interpretations of head specialization, acknowledges attention as a task-utility proxy and the absence of an optimized end-to-end pipeline, and qualifies OASST2 superiority by noting LagKV's advantage at the smallest budgets.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and newly discloses trace-collection requirements: 4,649 OASST2 samples, under two hours on 56 GPUs, approximately 1.2 TB of traces, and 11 GB per head. It documents physical compaction and JudgeQ reimplementation with matched training data. These substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing changes to the retained training setup.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds LOCRET and JudgeQ and distinguishes their query requirements and training procedures from KVP. References for RankNet and ListNet are added, while the Nemhauser citation accompanying the removed hardness statement disappears. The broader related-work taxonomy and positioning remain.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much existing prose remain. Targeted rewrites clarify reward definitions, compression protocols, generalization, and ablation explanations; the conclusion gains explicit limitations, an impact statement is added, and existing additional results move from Appendix A.4 to A.7.

P2.justification: v2 adds long-context, retrieval, JudgeQ, importance-distribution, rank-variance, and correlation displays. It redraws the supervised comparison, combines BoolQ and GovReport into Figure 4, and moves ARC-Challenge to the appendix. Existing Phi-4, qualitative, subtask, and per-head cost figures are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central rationale: broader supervised comparisons reveal budget-dependent tradeoffs, while 128K and repeated-compaction tests address previously limited evidence for long-context use. Corrected mathematics, resource disclosures, and explicit limitations improve assessability. Unexplained BoolQ revisions, single-sample head diagnostics, and missing end-to-end latency measurements remain limitations, but do not outweigh these gains.
